speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned waking up frightened; can you describe exactly what you see or hear during these episodes, and are you ever aware of any kicking or stiffening movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terrors (Sleep Terrors)

The absence of confusion upon waking and the ability to be consoled immediately after the episode are classic features distinguishing this from a nightmare or other sleep disorders. Since she appears tired the next day, we should investigate if there are any underlying sleep apnea issues or stressors affecting her rest.
